record_type_quote:
The replication included 101 couple dyads in the sample. This
was less than the target sample size of 166 couples, but more than used in the
original study (85 couples).

targets.authors: Vollmann, M., Antoniw, K., Hartung, F-M., & Renner, B.
targets.title: Social Support as a Mediator of the Stress Buffering Effect of Optimism: The Importance of Differentiating the Recipients’ and Providers’ Perspective.
targets.evidence_quote:
The claim selected for replication from Vollmann et al (2011) was:
"Among heterosexual romantic dyads, optimists (measured with the Life Orientation
Test revised) perceive lower levels of stress (measured with the Perceived Stress
Questionnaire)".
targets.outcome_quote:
The APIM model successfully replicated the effects of Vollmann et al. The actor
effect of optimism on perceived stress was b = -0.298, z= -9.529, p<.001 (p = .000
as reported by MPlus), showing that among dyad members, those with greater
optimism had lower perceived levels of stress. Thus, the replication of the claim was
successful according to the SCORE criteria.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall success verdict for the selected actor effect. Recruiting fewer dyads than planned is acknowledged but authors still conclude successful replication.

reasoning: Completed primary SCORE replication report by Tom Hostler and Sofia Persson; assigned file GUID and project identity verified through OSF API. New sample tests the 2011 published optimism–stress finding. Assigned 2025 metadata differs from the file upload date (2020), without an identity conflict.
